results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** The admissible origin $c$, the tensor objects $T_d=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and $T_{d+1}=T_d\otimes V$, the Schur functors $\pi_d,\pi_{d+1}$, and the residue functors on both sides.

[F1] The O-side residue functors are exact, biadjoint, preserve projectives and injectives, commute with restricted duality, and agree with the generalized Casimir eigencomponents; their $K_0$ operators are the integrable Fock Chevalley action ([[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], [[lem-residue-casimir-operators-give-local-affine-hecke-actions]], [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]).

[F2] The Hecke-side residue functors are exact, biadjoint, commute with the $*$-duality, and their operators are adjoint for the Cartan pairing ([[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]]).

[F3] The Schur functor is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples and sends standards to intrinsic Specht modules. Its tensor detector $T_d$ is prinjective, its Hecke endomorphism algebra is $B_d$, and its Whittaker image $U_d$ is a projective generator of the corresponding finite-W image category. There are natural identifications $\gamma_M:\pi_dM\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U_d,\mathrm{Wh}M)$ and the coherent tensor isomorphisms $\nu_M:\mathrm{Wh}(M\otimes V)\cong\mathrm{Wh}(M)\circledast V$, with $\mu_d:U_d\circledast V\cong U_{d+1}$ intertwining the tower generators. In the stable realization $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic algebra, while content projections give the supported blocks. Every category-O projective has a copresentation $0\to P\to T_1\to T_2$ with $T_1,T_2\in\operatorname{add}(T_d)$. These are the actual Whittaker/Morita, copresentation and tensor contracts of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]].

[F4] The parabolic and genuine category-O interfaces with the typed coset realization for admissible nonintegral origins ([[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).





**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The tensor identity $T_{d+1}=T_d\otimes V$, the actual Whittaker/Morita tensor data of [F3], and the two pairs of residue functors.

1.1 **Restriction uses the dual natural module.** For $N$ in the degree-$(d+1)$ summand and a basis $v_a$ of $V$ with dual basis $v^a$, tensor adjunction gives the natural map $\rho_N:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_{d+1},N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,N\otimes V^*)$, $\rho_N(h)(t)=\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$. Its inverse sends $g$ to $(t\otimes v)\mapsto(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_v)g(t)$. These maps are basis-independent by coevaluation and evaluation and commute with the first $d$ tower generators, acting on the $T_d$ factors. Thus they identify restriction of $\pi_{d+1}N$ with $\pi_d(N\otimes V^*)$ after the appropriate degree/block projection. The natural and dual natural modules are distinct $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-modules; no identification between them is used. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 **The induction map is an actual tensor map.** For $M$ of degree $d$, put $\tau_M:B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}\pi_dM\to\pi_{d+1}(M\otimes V)$, $b\otimes f\mapsto(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)\circ R_b$, where $R_b$ is the right action on $T_{d+1}$. The first $d$ generators act on $T_d$, so this expression is balanced over $B_d$ and is $B_{d+1}$-linear for the left-module convention; naturality follows by postcomposition. To prove it invertible, on the finite-W side form $\sigma_X(b\otimes g)=(g\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\circ\mu_d^{-1}\circ R_b$. For $X=U_d$ this is the regular-module isomorphism $B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}B_d\cong B_{d+1}$. It remains an isomorphism on finite sums and summands. Every finite-W image object has a finite projective presentation by summands of finite sums of $U_d$, and both sides are right exact: induction is right exact, tensoring with $V$ is exact and Hom from $U_d,U_{d+1}$ is exact. Passing to cokernels proves $\sigma_X$ invertible for all $X$. The coherent $\gamma,\nu,\mu$ square of [F3] sends $1\otimes f$ by either route to $(\mathrm{Wh}(f)\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\mu_d^{-1}$; $B_{d+1}$-linearity then makes the square commute on every $b\otimes f$. Consequently $\tau_M$ is invertible for every $M$. This presentation argument takes place in the finite-W image category, where $U_d$ is a full projective generator; it does not assert that $T_d$ is a full category-O generator. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The two residue projectors.** The tower's last dot on $T_d\otimes V$ is the tensor Casimir, with the normalization of [F1]. Hence $\tau$ intertwines its generalized-$i$ eigenprojector with the projector defining $f_i^{\mathcal O}$. On the dual tensor factor the adjunction mate is the dual Casimir: the flag calculation of [F1] gives eigenvalue $-n-i$ for the move $i+1\to i$, not $i$. Under $\rho$ the last-dot projector therefore corresponds to the generalized-$(-n-i)$ projector defining $e_i^{\mathcal O}$. Applying the source content projector $e_\alpha$ and target projector $e_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ to steps 1.1–1.2 gives $u_{\alpha,i}\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}N\cong\pi_\alpha e_i^{\mathcal O}N$ and $B_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{B_\alpha}\pi_\alpha M\cong\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}f_i^{\mathcal O}M$. Polynomial generalized-eigenspace projectors commute with these natural maps because the maps intertwine the operators, proving the asserted residue compatibility. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **Adjunction maps.** The first tensor unit is the coevaluation $m\mapsto\sum_a(m\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$, and the tensor counit is evaluation. The induction/restriction unit is $z\mapsto1\otimes z$, and the counit is $b\otimes z\mapsto bz$. Substituting these formulas into $\tau$ and $\rho$ gives the same composite maps, term by term: coevaluation is precisely the sum in $\rho$, and evaluation cancels that sum by $v^a(v_b)=\delta_{ab}$. Restricting the commuting squares by the content and residue projectors proves compatibility for $f_i\dashv e_i$. For the reverse adjunction use the biadjoint mate maps supplied by [F1] and the symmetric-trace reverse adjunction of [F2]; transport the latter through $\tau,\rho$. The transported evaluation and coevaluation pair is the O-side biadjoint pair, since its dot and crossing mates agree with those in [F1], with the same trace normalization. Equivalently the reverse unit and counit are the dual mates of the first pair, so the same squares commute. The two pairs are thus compared with their transported normalizations; this is stronger than asserting abstract uniqueness of adjoints across a quotient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.2 **Grothendieck operators and quotient.** Exactness of $\pi$ and of the residue functors makes the natural isomorphisms of step 2.1 induce $[f_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][f_i^{\mathcal O}]$ and $[e_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][e_i^{\mathcal O}]$. On $G_0$, the source simple-class basis shows that $\ker[\pi]$ is exactly the span of the off-standard simple classes, and the induced map from this quotient onto $G_0(H)$ is an isomorphism. No isomorphism from the entire category-O Grothendieck group is asserted. On split projective groups only $\operatorname{add}(T)$ is equivalent to Hecke projectives; an ambient off-standard projective need not have projective image. These distinctions leave the displayed operator equalities intact. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **The natural duality comparison.** The ordinary category-O duality $D$ uses matrix transpose and restricted weight-space duals. The product of the ground contravariant form and the natural-factor forms gives a nondegenerate detector form $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$; the Casimir, crossings and content projectors are self-adjoint. Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T_d)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$ and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(X,B_d)$ with the same twist. The form induces $\delta M\cong\pi_dDM$ by $f\mapsto[t\mapsto(m\mapsto(t,f(m)))]$: it is injective by nondegeneracy and surjective because $T_d$ is a sum of the self-dual projective covers/injective hulls of the same surviving simples, so both exact contravariant functors have identical dimensions on simple objects and hence on all finite-length objects. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi_d^*\cong\#$, while the symmetric trace of [F2] gives $\#\cong D_H$ by $h\mapsto\mathrm{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi_d^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The displayed form identity makes it balanced over $B_d$ and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi_d$ gives a natural transformation $\pi_d\to\pi_dD\pi_d^*\delta\cong\#\pi_dD$ between exact functors. It is an isomorphism on $T_d$ and hence on its finite sums and summands. Apply the copresentations in [F3] to prove it an isomorphism on every projective, by exactness and kernels; then apply projective presentations to prove it on every object, by cokernels. Dualizing yields the natural comparison $\pi_dD\cong D_H\pi_d$. The product forms, tensor evaluation and trace form are the same forms used for the dual adjunctions; consequently this comparison identifies their dual unit/counit squares. Since the residue projectors are self-adjoint, it also commutes with each $f_i,e_i$ separately. Thus $Df_i\cong f_iD$ and $De_i\cong e_iD$. None of this identifies the usual tensor dual $V^*$ with $V$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Filtrations and boundaries.** Applying exact $\pi$ to the O-side residue standard flags preserves their successive quotients, and the intertwined generalized-eigenvalue projectors select the corresponding residue pieces. Admissible nonintegral origins retain the typed coset realization of [F4]; an integral highest-weight Fock interpretation is used only on its actual integral residue component. All comparisons here are ungraded at parameter one. Together with steps 2.1–3.2 this proves the statement. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2, given] ∎

**Given:** The bounded-below tower $H^\Lambda$ of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the Fock data
and its four families as in
[[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], the exact
Schur quotient $\pi$ with its left adjoint $\pi^*$ as in
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and
[[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], and the assumption of the
Axiom of Choice used by the imported suppliers
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). We prove (i)-(v).

[F1] Every object of the category of finite-dimensional modules over a
finite-dimensional algebra has finite length, so the classes of simples form a
$\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0$, with composition multiplicities as coordinates
([[thm-finite-length-grothendieck-groups-have-simple-class-bases]]).

[F2] A class function on isomorphism classes that is additive on short exact
sequences factors uniquely through $G_0$, and an exact functor induces a
homomorphism of $G_0$ functorially
([[thm-grothendieck-group-universal-properties-and-functoriality]]).

[F3] The Axiom of Choice holds: every family of nonempty sets has a choice
function ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The Schur quotient and its simple images.** Assume AC ([F3]) as the imported suppliers do. In the admissible stable realization, the exact Schur quotient $\pi$ of [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]] is the Serre quotient killing exactly the simples $L(A)$ with $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$; it satisfies $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$ for the intrinsic Specht modules and $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, these $D(A)$ being pairwise nonisomorphic and exhausting the simples of $\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda)$, while $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$. By [F1] the classes $[D(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))$. The ingredients are the Schur-functor image theorem, exactness of $\pi$ and the double-centralizer/quotient description of [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]]. [F1, F3, given, construct]

1.2 **The Fock side of the dictionary.** On the Fock side the normalized highest projection $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}$ is the linear map with $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=D_A$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_A=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, and $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}M_B=S_B$ with $M_B=\sum_{A}d_{A,B}(s)L_A$ and $S_B=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A$ at source parameter $1$; the vectors $\{D_A\}$ span the full integral costandard lattice $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ and the vectors $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ form the standard monomial basis of that lattice, a second integral basis. These are the definitions and the standard-monomial basis theorem of [[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]] and [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]], together with the O-side dictionary $[L(A)]\mapsto L_A$, $[P(A)]\mapsto P_A$, $[T(A)]\mapsto T_A$ of [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]. [given, construct]

1.3 **The O-side Grothendieck group is the integral Fock module.** At parameter one the parabolic category-O Grothendieck group is identified with the integral Fock module by $[M(A)]\mapsto M_A$, with $\dim\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)=\langle[P],[N]\rangle$ and $\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB}$, by [[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]; here $M(A)$, $L(A)$, $P(A)$ are the generalized standard, simple and projective objects of the genuine block $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]. [given, construct]

2.1 **The identification of $G_0$ with the costandard lattice.** Define $\Phi\colon G_0(\mathrm{Rep}(H^\Lambda))\to V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Z}$ on the basis of step 1.1 by $\Phi([D(A)])=D_A$. This is a well-defined group isomorphism because both sides are free $\mathbb Z$-modules with the same basis set $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$: on the module side by [F1] and step 1.1, on the Fock side by step 1.2, which exhibits $\{D_A\}$ as a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the FULL integral costandard lattice and makes no integral ground-generation claim. This proves (i) for the simple classes and, together with step 1.2, identifies $\Phi([S(B)])$ with $S_B$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, construct]

2.2 **The Specht classes.** For the intrinsic Specht module $S(B)=\pi(N(B))$ of step 1.1, apply the exact functor $\pi$ to a Jordan–Hölder composition series of $N(B)$; exactness and [F2] give $[S(B)]=\sum_{A}[N(B):L(A)]\,[D(A)]$ in $G_0$, the sum running over the simples, i.e. over $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by step 1.1. The multiplicity $[N(B):L(A)]$ equals the Fock coefficient $d_{A,B}(1)$ of step 1.2 by the O-side multiplicity dictionary of step 1.3 and the Schur-image theorem of step 1.1. Hence $\Phi([S(B)])=\sum_{A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda}d_{A,B}(1)D_A=S_B$, and the square submatrix on standard columns is unitriangular, so $\{S_B:B\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda\}$ is an integral basis; this completes (i). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, F2, algebra]

2.3 **Divided-power integral forms.** The lower library global vectors $G_{\mathrm{low}}(A)=T_{A^\uparrow}=s^{-a(\alpha)}P_A$ and the form-dual upper vectors $G_{\mathrm{up}}(A)=s^{a(\alpha)}D_A$ with $a(\alpha)=(2\Lambda-\alpha,\alpha)/2$ span integral forms on which the divided powers of the Chevalley generators act integrally, by [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]]; at parameter one the standard lattice is therefore generated over $\mathbb Z$ by its ground vector $P_{A_\Lambda}$ under the divided-power operators $f_i^{(n)}$, while the costandard lattice is its full weightwise $C_0$-dual: at $s=1$, $C_0(P_A,D_B)=\delta_{AB}$ identifies it with $\bigoplus_\alpha\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(V(\Lambda)_{\mathbb Z,\alpha},\mathbb Z)$. In particular it is stable under divided powers, since the $e_i^{(n)}$ and $f_i^{(n)}$ are adjoint and preserve the lower lattice. Nondegeneracy identifies their rational scalar extensions, but does not identify the two integral lattices. The ground-generation use is the actual definition $V_{\mathcal A}(\Lambda)=U^-_{\mathcal A}v_\Lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], specialized at one; it concerns the standard lattice only. This gives the divided-power clause of (ii) and separates the two lattices. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 **Residue operators.** The residue functors $e_i^H,f_i^H$ are exact, so they induce endomorphisms of $G_0$ by [F2]. The natural intertwining isomorphisms $f_i^H\pi\cong\pi f_i^O$ and $e_i^H\pi\cong\pi e_i^O$ of [[thm-category-o-translation-intertwines-residue-induction-and-restriction]], together with the category-O Chevalley action of [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]], show that $[\pi]$ is a module map. Steps 1.1–2.2 identify its kernel with the span of the off-standard simple classes, precisely the kernel of the Fock projection. Thus the induced quotient map $\Phi$ intertwines $e_i,f_i$, proving the ordinary Chevalley clause of (ii). No head, socle or indecomposability assertion is inferred merely from exactness of a quotient. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, F2, given, algebra]

3.2 **Level zero.** If the level is $0$, then $\Lambda=0$, the only simple is the ground class in degree $0$, and the tower is $H^\Lambda_0=\mathbb C$ by the level-$0$ convention of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]]; then $G_0=\mathbb Z[D(\varnothing)]\cong\mathbb ZD_\varnothing$ is the ground line alone, with both lattices equal to the ground line and every residue operator zero. This is the level-$0$ clause of (v). [step 1.1, step 2.1, given]

4.1 **Crystal reachability and composition factors.** The source upper ground component is exactly $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ by [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]]. The normalized highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space, so over $\mathbb Q$ it identifies the full costandard lattice's scalar extension with the irreducible highest module. Its highest vector therefore generates that module under lowering divided powers. Consequently every basis vector $D_A$ is a rational linear combination of lowering words applied to the ground vector. By step 3.1 each ordinary lowering word is the class of the corresponding exact residue-word module, with nonnegative simple-class coefficients by [F1]. If $D(A)$ occurred in none of these modules, every such word and every rational linear combination would have zero $D_A$ coefficient, contrary to the coefficient one in $D_A$. Thus some residue word contains $D(A)$ as a composition factor. This proves (iv) without requiring integral costandard generation or transport of head and socle through the quotient. [step 2.1, step 2.3, step 3.1, F1, given, algebra]

4.2 **The maps for arbitrary consecutive $I$.** Fix a finite set of contents and residue words. Choose $J=[k,r]$ so that $[k,r+1]$ contains every charge and $J$ contains every intermediate root support; decrease $k$ further to reach the needed stable range. The Hecke-side map is literally the identity on $H_d(m)e_\alpha$: its spectral idempotent is the same sum over words of content $\alpha$, independently of whether the ambient supported interval is $I$ or $J$. It therefore fixes the intrinsic residue corner $u_{\alpha,i}$ and the bimodules defining $e_i,f_i$. On tableaux the lower transition adjoins the prescribed ground entries to every column, and the upper transition regards the same entries in a larger alphabet with no new top entries. Removing that common tail is the inverse on the selected weight. Column ground differences, hence intrinsic Specht partitions, are unchanged. The actual finite-cut compatibility of [[thm-standard-tableau-monomials-form-a-basis-of-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule]] and [[thm-the-highest-weight-fock-submodule-has-the-qg-global-bases]] gives $D_{\jmath A}=\jmath D_A$, $S_{\jmath B}=\jmath S_B$, $P_{\jmath A}=\jmath P_A$ and commuting normalized highest projections. Thus both upper and lower lattices are identified by their full bases, not just their rational spans. On overlapping cuts these maps compose by adjoining/removing the same ground entries and by the intrinsic Hecke identity; the normalized projections agree by highest-vector uniqueness. Every content, vector and finite residue word fits such a cut. Applying steps 1.1–6.1 there and taking the compatible weightwise direct sum proves all clauses for arbitrary admitted $I$. No full degree algebra is identified with a proper supported cut. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.3, step 3.1, given, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Rational ground cyclicity.** The normalized $E/F$-contravariant highest form is nondegenerate on each finite weight space. Thus its weightwise duality identifies $V(\Lambda)^*_{\mathbb Q}$, interpreted as the direct sum of the costandard weight spaces, with the irreducible rational highest module. The ground vector maps to the normalized highest vector; its orbit under lowering divided powers therefore spans every weight space, as used in step 4.1. This proves the rational clause of (iii). The full unrestricted algebraic dual of an infinite-dimensional module is not used. [step 2.3, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, algebra]

6.1 **The rank-one index-two witness.** Take $I=\{0\}$ and $\Lambda=2\Lambda_0$. The supported degree-one block is $B_0=\mathbb C[x]/x^2$ and the supported degree-two block is $M_2(\mathbb C)$, with its simple represented by $x_1=N=E_{12}$, $s_1=-(E_{12}+E_{21})$ and $x_2=-N$. The first dot is not zero on that simple. The actual residue Ind/Res dimensions give $fD_{00}=2D_{01}$, $fD_{01}=D_{11}$ and $eD_{01}=D_{00}$, $eD_{11}=2D_{01}$, with the end actions zero. Their divided squares give $f^{(2)}D_{00}=D_{11}$ and $e^{(2)}D_{11}=D_{00}$. Therefore $\mathbb ZD_{00}\oplus2\mathbb ZD_{01}\oplus\mathbb ZD_{11}$ is stable under $e,f$ and all their divided powers, contains the ground vector and excludes $D_{01}$. This is a proper integral costandard submodule, whereas over $\mathbb Q$ division by two recovers $D_{01}$. Degree one is not called a corner sitting inside degree two. [step 2.3, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 **Conclusion.** Step 2.1 identifies $G_0$ with the full integral costandard lattice and step 2.2 computes the Specht classes, proving (i); step 2.3 gives the divided-power integral forms and step 3.1 identifies the residue operators with the Chevalley operators, proving (ii); step 5.1 proves rational ground cyclicity, step 2.3 proves integral ground generation of the standard lattice and step 6.1 exhibits the index-two failure of integral costandard cyclicity, proving (iii) and its sharpness; step 4.1 proves the crystal reachability statement (iv); and step 3.2 (level zero) together with steps 5.1 and 6.1 separates the rational-cyclicity and categorical reachability conclusions from integral costandard cyclicity, as asserted in (v); step 4.2 supplies the arbitrary-$I$ maps and full integral extension. No step identifies $\{D_A\}$ with the standard divided-power lattice, and no integral costandard generation is used. [step 2.2, step 2.3, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 4.2, step 3.2, given] ∎

**Given:** The inherited Axiom of Choice and the tower $H^\Lambda$ and its block-wise Grothendieck groups as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-tower-and-residue-functors]], the exact Schur
quotient $\pi$ with right-exact left adjoint $\pi^*$ of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], the
Schur-image identifications $\pi(N(A))=S(A)$, $\pi(L(A))=D(A)$,
$\pi(P(A))=Y(A)$ for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ and
$\pi^*\pi(P(A))=P(A)$ of
[[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]],
and the Fock dictionary $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}(P_A)=P_A$, $\pi_{\mathrm{Fock}}L_B=D_B$
at parameter one. We prove (i)-(v).

[F1] Finite-dimensional projective modules over a finite-dimensional algebra
have a free split Grothendieck group on the classes of the projective covers
([[thm-finite-dimensional-algebra-projective-classes-form-a-split-k-zero-basis]]).

[F2] On object pairs the Cartan pairing is
$\langle[P],[M]\rangle=\dim_k\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)$, its descent to
$K_0\times G_0$ and the duality of the two bases are proved in
[[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]] (definition:
[[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]).

[F3] Exact adjoint functors acting compatibly on projectives induce adjoint maps
of Grothendieck groups for the Hom pairing
([[thm-adjoint-exact-functors-induce-adjoint-grothendieck-operators]]).



**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The split $K_0$ basis of covers.** Every simple finite-dimensional $H^\Lambda$-module has a projective cover, unique up to isomorphism, and the classes $[Y(A)]$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, of the covers of the simples $D(A)$ of [[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-g-zero-is-the-dual-highest-weight-module]] form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of the split Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional projective modules; this is [F1] applied block by block and summed over $\alpha\in Q^+$. [F1, given, construct]

1.2 **The left adjoint on projectives.** The Schur quotient $\pi$ has a left adjoint $\pi^*$ which is right exact on all modules and sends $H$-projectives to category-O projectives; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$ one has $\pi^*(Y(A))=P(A)$ and $\pi\pi^*(Y(A))=Y(A)$, so $\pi^*$ recovers the standard-labelled prinjectives, and its exactness on arbitrary modules is not needed. These are the statements of [[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]. [given, construct]
